chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about al-Mut'ah, and he said:
It was revealed in the Quran: 'So for whatever you have taken of them [in temporary marriage], give them their dowries as an obligation.'
And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) and its financial rulings?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar provides the foundational Shia argument for the validity of al-Mut'ah by linking it directly to the 'Ujrah' (dowry) mentioned in Surah An-Nisa, verse 24. It clarifies that the obligatory payment is the minimum requirement, while any additional mutual agreement (taradhin) is permissible, a view supported by the majority of Shia jurists who consider the verse abrogated in its prohibition aspect but retained for the permission aspect.
